insights.title: Standard exponentials,reciprocal-linear and affine trig primitives
insights.teaching_comparison: GoldieC5teaches affine exponentials/reciprocals then standard trig forms;YMC12separates exponential,log-validityand trig sections before exact finite evaluation. YM explicitly asks ordinary-ln validity in6/Try6; Goldie explanations and the independent answer checks retain absolute-log primitives on both real components.
insights.examination_comparison: 2021P2Q2/9(a),2022P2Q8and2024P2Q5(b)anchor standard-form integration. Exactln(a)or exact trigonometric values are actual response demands; a decimal substitute is not automatically equivalent marking evidence. Original report precision rules remain authoritative.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: A09/C15bound the listed affine forms; general substitution is not required. The entry branch compensates one inner coefficient; harder originals require algebraic expansion,correct ordinary-log branch or a requested single-log final form. E09/C09supply reverse differentiation foundations.
insights.pitfalls: YM8(b)crosses a pole and its finite endpoint answer is invalid. A wholly negative denominator interval such asTry8(b)is valid with absolute logs. Negative inner slopes flip primitive signs; finite root or reciprocal endpoints must be checked before evaluation.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM has more explicit validity/answer-form drills; Goldie has more mixed source contexts. General nonlinear-log integrals inGoldieC8remain extra even when their answer is verified. Both books contain valid alternative forms that differ by a constant.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose standard primitive,proper definite,requested-log-form and explicit-domain branches. Validate primitives against the original integrand and intervals independently; preserve signed values,exactness and source defects rather than adopting keys blindly.

insights.title: Supplied reverse-derivative scaffolds and method boundaries
insights.teaching_comparison: Goldie8Activity2explicitly supplies products to differentiate and rearrange before integrating;YM7Example12andC12Example17/Try17derive a suitable reciprocal derivative before reverse use. Those scaffolds make the route different from asking the learner to invent general parts/substitution. A derivative-at-point alone does not automatically supply the required primitive.
insights.examination_comparison: 2021P2Q5(b),2024P2Q4(b)and2025P2Q10(b)anchor use of a preceding/given derivative. Official criteria decide what the prescribed reuse earns. Extra-methodGoldie tasks cannot become equivalent simply because an8227alternative gives the same numeric result.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E09/C09/A09bound reverse differentiation; general substitution is not required. Easier branches match a supplied derivative directly; harder ones require scaling/rearrangement and a remaining standard primitive. Keep the actual supplied information and hence edge as difficulty boundaries.
insights.pitfalls: Goldie8Prompt4blanket claim about2/(x squared-1)is false under its already taught extra methods; the key only rejects one substitution. A printed method claim is source evidence to audit,not an unquestionable rule. CAS additive constants do not make two equivalent primitives conflicting answers.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Goldie has explicit parts motivation and many forced methods outside8227; YM stays closer to its listed forms but still uses reverse-derived sec/cot primitives. Source method compliance and mathematical validity are separate axes.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose genuine derivative-hence branches with exact linkage and independent differentiate-back checks. Preserve forced-method exclusions and label an adapted in-scope version explicitly; do not erase original method instructions.

insights.title: Identity choice,squared trig expressions and geometric integration
insights.teaching_comparison: Goldie5Bdevelops square reduction,compound products and scaffolded higher-power forms;YM14/16/23separates freely chosen identities from prove-then-hence and complementary-integral deduction. Goldie8unforced finite trig products can be reduced by derived identities; optional substitution in its solution does not make the original extra-scope.
insights.examination_comparison: 2021P2Q9(b),2022P2Q3(c),2023P2Q5(b)and2024P2Q6(a)(b)anchor transformed trig integration,area and volume. A supporting squared-cosine primitive does not cover the whole supplied-region or rotation question. Official scheme alternatives remain distinct from textbook working.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: C14/C15/A09explicitly name identities to facilitate squared-trig integration. Entry tasks use one half-angle replacement; harder sources expand a mixed square,repeat reduction or derive a finite triple identity. The derived identity is not an extra memorisation requirement.
insights.pitfalls: Expand the whole square including its cross term and double the original inner argument. YM24(a)has equivalent primitives differing by a constant; the checker now fixes a deterministic independent integration algorithm. Rotation requires the squared whole radius and actual original region.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM provides repeated exact,henceand area/volume chains; Goldie has wider optional/forced-method contrasts. Repeated source question occurrences are not extra family breadth. Diagram boundaries or requested maxima may end a region before its first intercept.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose free-choice,provided-identity,proof-henceand geometric branches with explicit original bounds/axes. Preserve connected parts and branch-specific method evidence; check diagrams and exact primitives independently.

insights.title: Trapezium ordinates,weights,precision and tabulated applications
insights.teaching_comparison: GoldieC5explicitly explores many widths,individual constituent trapezia,piestimation and tabulated train motion. YMC12first contrasts the exactx squared area with a four-strip estimate,then uses prescribed two/three/four intervals and literal decimal/significant-figure outputs. A common-log node evaluation is not a change-of-base question.
insights.examination_comparison: 2023P2Q6(a)(b)and2025P2Q4(a)anchor the actual numerical method. A correct exact integral or calculator numerical value does not demonstrate the requested trapezium calculation. The connected logarithmic comparison in2023is additional to merely estimating the integral.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: A10/C15bound trapezium applications; begin with given ordinates then derive nodes for a stated interval count. Harder tasks add data units,complementary area,required final answer form or multiple refinements. More strips alone are not a higher Bloom classification.
insights.pitfalls: nintervals needn+1ordinates and doubled interior weights. Keep internal precision before final rounding;YM24Tryasks2sf0.90,not a display that loses the trailing zero. Exact values and estimates must retain different labels.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Goldie has richer refinement/data/model-limitation work;YMoffers many exam-style given curves. Goldie5C6shows coarse-node aliasing,so stable repeated estimates do not establish correctness. The train table lacks complete between-sample behaviour.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose function/table branches,explicit node/weight records,literal precision and independent reference computation. Retain original response units and error/model limitations; do not count each width or curve coefficient as a new type.

insights.title: Integrand sketches and justified trapezium bias
insights.teaching_comparison: Goldie links repeated sketches,straight-top approximations and a mixed-curvature no-universal-direction example;its closing investigation checks left/right/midpoint claims with counterexamples. YM distinguishes supplied diagrams from required sketches,and asks chord-position explanations after numeric estimates. The actual finite integration interval matters more than the full natural-domain graph.
insights.examination_comparison: 2023P2Q6(c)(d)requires a learner sketch and an explanation referring back to the estimate;2025P2Q4(b)combines a reciprocal graph with over/under reasoning. Numeric agreement alone does not satisfy that visual/explanatory demand. The record retains credited features rather than claiming a generic image response is enough.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: C15explicitly uses simple sketch graphs for over/under conclusions;A10includes trapezium applications. Start with a single-concavity finite interval; harder sources involve complement bias reversal,changing curvature or aliasing. General universal error theorems are not invented scope.
insights.pitfalls: An asymptote outside the integration interval does not invalidate the proper estimate. A maximum alone does not decide chord bias. Area-complement subtraction reverses error direction. A drawing without a reason is not a complete explanation.
insights.gaps_and_representations: Goldie supplies uncertainty/counterexample variety;YMhas clear estimate-sketch-bias chains and source cue defects. Worksheet plots,required learner sketches and given diagrams must remain distinct. Left/right/midpoint enrichment is not automatically an8227requirement.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose consistent curve/node/chord models,part-specific sketch features and an explicit explanation criterion. Test the actual interval and all region complements; keep inconclusive mixed-curvature cases honest instead of forcing an over/under answer.
